title: KV retention profiles and version gating for long-context model onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: As we onboard larger open models and variants, performance for very long sequences varies widely by architecture, quantization, and KV cache retention strategy. Current onboarding collects single-point latency/throughput numbers and an aggregate KV warmup metric. This ticket builds an explicit pipeline to publish per-model 'KV retention profiles' (how beneficial and costly it is to retain KV entries across request boundaries for different sequence distributions) and a version-gating signal so runtime and Console can pin or suggest model variants for customers with heavy long-context usage.
goals: 1) Define and compute KV retention profiles per model+quantization+sequence-distribution. 2) Emit a profile artifact to the model catalog for use by routing/version-pinning. 3) Add a lightweight gating decision that prevents automatic rollout of a model version for customers with >X% long-context traffic unless profile passes thresholds. 4) Create dashboards and alerts to detect profile regressions.
acceptance_criteria:
- A nightly profiling job generates a JSON profile per model variant with: retention benefit curve, cold-start penalty, median tail-latency at 5 sequence buckets, and a profile quality score.
- Model catalog UI shows the latest profile and a human-readable recommendation (e.g., 'recommended for long-context', 'use q4_0 variant for latency-critical').
- Routing policy can query catalog and apply version gating: if customer long-context ratio > 30% and profile quality < threshold, block auto-rollout.
- End-to-end test coverage and a canary run on internal dedicated pool that validates rollback behavior when gating blocks.
- Documentation for SRE and Solutions teams on how to override gating and how to interpret profiles.
design_notes:
- Profile pipeline will drive a staged workload generator: synthetic long-tail sequences + sampled real-session prefixes. We will compute delta metrics for retention windows (0=no cross-request retention, 1=retain 1k tokens, 2=retain 5k, 3=retain full). Retention benefit curve = tokens_saved_per_second vs extra memory and KV lookup overhead.
- Use statistically robust sampling: bootstrap confidence intervals for tail latencies. Persist profiles as immutable artifacts with schema version.
- Version gating is advisory by default; enterprise tenants with MLPolicies can opt-in blocking. Gating decisions will be logged to audit logs.
- Performance overhead: the nightly job must be parallel and bounded (max N GPU-hours per day). We'll sample subset of models initially (top 50 by traffic).
- Telemetry: new metrics kvcache.retention.benefit, kvcache.retention.overhead, model.profile.quality, gating.block.count.
implementation_plan:
1) Data harness: extend perf-harness to generate long-context workloads and retention modes (owner: eng-perf). 2) Compute infra: new profiling lambda + job runner to submit to dedicated profiling pool and aggregate outputs (owner: infra). 3) Catalog publisher: API + storage location for profile artifacts and versioned schema (owner: model-catalog). 4) Console and routing integration: expose profile and gating flag in Console + routing policy check (owner: runtime-routing). 5) Rollout: internal canary -> beta customers -> global.
Links: Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/KV+Retention+Profiles, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1982, perf dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/kv-retention/profiles
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for profile schema and aggregation.
- Integration: run profiling job end-to-end for a small model and verify artifact published to catalog.
- Canary: enable gating for internal team (team id: redwood-internal) and assert that an incoming model rollout that would be gated is correctly blocked and audit-logged.
- Regression: nightly comparison of new profile vs last-known with statistical delta thresholds; alert if profile quality drops >10%.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Profiling job could consume excessive GPU-hours. Mitigation: start with top-50 models and enforce strict parallelism and timeouts. Risk: False-positive gating blocks customer rollouts. Mitigation: make gating advisory for first 4 weeks and add override flow with audit trail. Risk: Profile schema changes. Mitigation: versioned artifacts and migration tooling.
rollout_and_observability:
- Phase 1: internal profiling + publish artifacts to dev catalog.
- Phase 2: Console UI surfaces recommendations; routing consults profile but does not enforce.
- Phase 3: Enable gating for a small set of customers, monitor gating.block.count and support tickets.
- Dashboards to monitor sample size, CI intervals, retention benefit, gating hits.
- Pager rule: if nightly job fails >2 days or profile count drops >30% without explanation.
notes: This ticket intentionally separates retention profiling from KV prefetch policies; later follow-ups will convert retention curves into concrete caching presets per model. Also coordinate with PM for customer communication before changing default rollout behavior.
